correctness.rationale: Exact remainders modulo Phi30 give a positive linear functional with zero weights on indices 0..4 and 15..19 and strictly positive weights on 5..14. Nonnegativity kills the middle ten coefficients; X^15=-1 modulo Phi30 forces equality of the two remaining blocks. Phi30(X^(2^h))=Phi_(30*2^h)(X), residue-class decomposition lifts the assertion to all h. A three-term 3-gon at exactly 20*2^h proves the sharp boundary, and the zero-one count follows from disjoint blocks. The attached standalone verifier reconstructs all pivotal finite identities and checks the relevant boundary witnesses; finite experiments are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The checked 2026 primary paper proves only a minimum diameter and quantitative mass proximity, not the exact nonnegative subcritical cone for the three-prime order 30 or its dyadic tower. The 2012 even-index minimum theorem and 2000 minimal-sum/weight classifications likewise do not assert or imply a coefficientwise exclusion on the full interval. An explicit twenty-position dual certificate supplies the missing structural assertion. Database and own-history search identified no matching implication; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Unindexed historical treatments of positive vanishing 30th-root relations may implicitly include the precise arc cutoff.
The normal positive-root cancellation problem for real weights is broader than actual real polynomial divisibility and is not covered here.

value.rationale: At the smallest squarefree order with three prime factors, the known minimum diameter only describes one extreme ray. This sharp theorem identifies all nonnegative real coefficient multiples across the full interval 1/2 <= D/N < 2/3; it locates the first possible non-antipodal arc and enumerates binary masks exactly by diameter. The relation to minimal vanishing sums at order 30 and to sharp general bounds is natural and explicitly motivated. It is a structural infinite-family result, not just a known table or a tiny numerical improvement.
